label: Day Lighting
description: Daylight keys — sun angle, cloud cover and daylight-balanced studio looks, each with its shadow behavior spelled out.

items.name: golden-hour
items.text: The last full hour before sunset, sunlight arriving nearly horizontal and amber-warm, raking extremely long soft-edged shadows and wrapping every contour in glow.

items.name: backlit-rim-light
items.text: Strong direct backlight from a low sun, a brilliant rim burning along the subject's upper edges while the camera side falls into open readable shadow, flare held just off-axis.

items.name: volumetric-god-rays
items.text: Hazy atmospheric daylight, the sun hidden behind broken cloud or canopy, visible volumetric beams slanting through moisture-laden air and pooling in bright patches on the ground.

items.name: overcast-softbox
items.text: A bright, uniformly overcast sky acting as one giant softbox: even wraparound light, shadows reduced to a soft contact core under the subject, colors reading true without specular glare.

items.name: high-key-studio
items.text: Flawless high-key studio daylight, massive overlapping softboxes on a white cyclorama dissolving shadows to a faint grounding shade directly beneath the subject.

items.name: hard-spotlight
items.text: A single hard-edged spotlight in an otherwise dark studio, one focused beam with knife-edge shadow cutoff and steep circular falloff into black.

items.name: storm-shafts
items.text: Gathering storm clouds stacked charcoal-dark overhead, intense shafts of sunlight breaking through gaps and igniting the scene in moving high-contrast pools.

items.name: open-shade
items.text: Open shade just beyond the sunline, the subject lit only by blue skylight and ground bounce, a soft directional wash with cool clean color and no squinting highlights.

items.name: backlit-bounce-fill
items.text: Low sun behind the subject as a rim light with a large silver bounce lifting the shadow side from camera left, the classic daylight sandwich of burning edge and readable face.

items.name: noon-toplight
items.text: Cloudless noon sun almost directly overhead, hard top-light compressing shadows into short dense pools beneath every overhang, specular glare standing on the horizontal surfaces while the verticals fall half a stop darker.

items.name: veiled-sun
items.text: Sun filtering through a thin high veil of cirrus, still clearly directional but its shadow edges widened to a soft penumbra, highlights tamed enough to hold detail — the whole sky working as one stretched silk.

items.name: urban-canyon-bounce
items.text: Direct sun blocked by tall buildings, the subject lit instead by a glass tower bouncing a broad second sun into the shade, a soft warm directional wash carrying a faint grid of window reflections.
